The model FilePathField already accepts a callable path. Its formfield() resolves it with `self.path() if callable(self.path) else self.path`. deconstruct() writes `self.path` into the migration kwargs unchanged, so a callable is kept as a reference instead of being resolved to a machine-specific string. I did not check the forms.FilePathField side or run anything.

For multiline RawSQL, `search(sql)` therefore captured only the last line before ASC/DESC. `get_order_by()` then treated clauses with identical last lines as duplicates. The code already has the fix: the pattern `^(.*)\s(?:ASC|DESC).*` is compiled with `re.MULTILINE | re.DOTAL

The code already handles memoryview. `HttpResponseBase.make_bytes` in `django/http/response.py` converts `bytes` and `memoryview` values with `bytes(value)`. The `content` setter also treats `memoryview` as a single value rather than iterating over it, so `HttpResponse(memoryview(b"My Content")).content` gives `b'My Content'`. I read the `make_bytes` lines but did not run the example.
The fast-delete path in Collector.delete (single instance, no dependencies) now clears the PK with setattr(instance, model._meta.pk.attname, None) after the delete query runs.

The migration wraps the Permission update in transaction.atomic() and catches IntegrityError (when permissions for the recreated proxy model's content type already exist), writing a warning instead of failing.

The `__main__` module (usually manage.py) is now added to the watched files in `iter_modules_and_files`. It has no `__spec__`, so the code falls back to `module.__file__` when the module name is `__main__` or `__mp_main__`. Without that, manage.py was skipped by the `__spec__ is None` check.

SCRIPT_NAME support for STATIC_URL and MEDIA_URL is implemented in `LazySettings._add_script_prefix`. `LazySettings.__getattr__` calls it for those two settings and caches the result. It prepends `get_script_prefix()` to relative values and leaves values starting with http://, https:// or / unchanged.

The fix is in `iter_modules_and_files` in `django/utils/autoreload.py`. It wraps `path.exists()` in a `try/except ValueError`. If a path contains an embedded null byte (for example from a network filesystem), it logs a debug message and skips that file instead of crashing the reloader.

Any table name used by more than one model is then reported as "db_table '%s' is used by multiple models". If that length is greater than max_length, it returns the error fields.E009: "'max_length' is too small to fit the longest value in 'choices' (%d characters)." EnumSerializer.serialize in django/db/migrations/serializer.py now serializes enum members by name, e.g. `module.Status['GOOD']`, rather than by value (`Status('Good')`). This is the fix the issue asks for. Translating the value no longer breaks old migrations. For Flag enums, the members are joined with " | ". I read the code but did not run it.

In MigrationAutodetector.generate_altered_fields, the ForeignKey single to_field case: when the target field (rename_key + remote_field.field_name) is in self.renamed_fields, the code repoints new_field.remote_field.model and remote_field.field_name to the old field's values, so the AlterField comparison/deconstruct handles the renamed PK's to_field.

Field.contribute_to_class() only sets get_FOO_display() if the class doesn't already define it. The check is `if "get_%s_display" % self.name not in cls.__dict__:`, and it sits inside `if self.choices is not None:`. A get_FOO_display() you define on the model is therefore no longer overwritten. The check looks only at cls.__dict__, so methods inherited from a parent class don't count.

The "database is locked" error comes from `test_db_signature()` in the SQLite `DatabaseCreation`. The signature has to include each alias's own TEST NAME when the test database is a file. Otherwise `default` and `other` get the same signature, and the test runner treats `other` as a mirror of `default`. Both aliases then share one database file. Field.contribute_to_class now sets get_FOO_display only if the class's own __dict__ doesn't define it (not inherited methods), so child classes can override inherited choices.

The E004 check, `check_language_settings_consistent`, already calls `get_supported_language_variant(settings.LANGUAGE_CODE)` and only returns E004 when that raises LookupError. `get_supported_language_variant` falls back to the base language, so "de-at" resolves to "de" and shouldn't raise E004. This corpus already has the fix, and I did not run it to confirm.

The codebase already contains the fix. `BaseDatabaseCreation.deserialize_db_from_string` wraps the deserialize and save loop in `atomic(using=self.connection.alias)`. Inside that block it disables constraint checks and then runs `check_constraints` afterwards, so a model that references a foreign key can be saved before the model it references.

It returns `{model._meta.label: count}` unconditionally, so a count of 0 still produces a dictionary entry, e.g. `(0, {'my_app.BlockLibrary': 0})`. StaticFilesHandlerMixin.get_response_async, which calls self.serve through sync_to_async and turns Http404 into a response with response_for_exception.

slugify() in django/utils/text.py now strips leading and trailing dashes and underscores. The final line collapses runs of dashes and whitespace into one dash, then calls .strip("-_"). I only read the code and didn't run it. By that logic, "___This is a test ---" gives "this-is-a-test".

The error is raised in Query.check_filterable in django/db/models/sql/query.py. It raises NotSupportedError when the filter value has a `resolve_expression` attribute and its `filterable` attribute is falsy. A model instance with a field named `filterable` set to False meets both conditions, which causes the reported error. The check also recurses into `get_source_expressions()`.

Otherwise it compares `hash(self) == hash(other)`. `__hash__` is built from message, code and params for a single error. For error lists and dicts it is presumably order-independent, but I didn't read that part of `__hash__`.

The fix is already in `Query.resolve_lookup_value`. For a namedtuple (detected with `hasattr(type_, "_make")`), it now expands the resolved values with `type_(*values)`. Other list and tuple types still get `type_(values)`.

In ManagementUtility.execute(), the CommandParser is now created with prog=self.prog_name (with usage="%(prog)s subcommand [options] [args]", add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False), so %(prog)s refers to the computed prog_name instead of sys.argv[0].

InlineModelAdmin.__init__ in django/contrib/admin/options.py now derives verbose_name_plural from the Inline's verbose_name when only verbose_name is set. It uses format_lazy("{}s", self.verbose_name). If neither is set, it falls back to the model's Meta verbose_name_plural.
Signal.send_robust() now logs receiver exceptions via the helper `_log_robust_failure`, which calls `logger.error(..., exc_info=err)`. The sync and async except clauses call this helper.

Q._combine in django/db/models/query_utils.py no longer deepcopies the operand. When self is empty it returns other.copy() (line 59). Node.__copy__ in django/utils/tree.py is a shallow copy, so a dict_keys child is never pickled.

The Q-side check in Q._combine is the place that decides this. Q._combine used to raise TypeError for any operand that wasn't a Q. In this code it accepts any operand whose `conditional` attribute is truthy, so Q() & Exists(...) no longer raises. When Q is empty it returns other.copy(). I did not run it, and I did not check how Exists gets `conditional`.

FormSet.full_clean() creates `_non_form_errors` as an ErrorList with `error_class="nonform"`. It does this when the errors list is first initialised, and again when a ValidationError is caught (line 458). The class is added at formsets.py:401 for the initial list.

Query.add_deferred_loading in django/db/models/sql/query.py: when defer() removes all names from an existing only() set, the branch clears deferred loading (loading all fields) and only sets deferred (new_only, True) for names not in the existing only set; the logic at lines 2329-2334 governs this behavior.

MessageEncoder.default in cookie.py now checks `if obj.extra_tags is not None:` instead of the truthiness of extra_tags. An empty-string extra_tags is therefore appended to the encoded message and survives the round trip. I did not run the reproduction snippet.

BaseCommand.create_parser sets the parser's formatter_class to DjangoHelpFormatter by default (kwargs.setdefault("formatter_class", DjangoHelpFormatter)). It also passes self.help as the description. That formatter reflows the description, which is why the newlines and indentation in help are lost. A command can pass its own formatter_class through create_parser kwargs to change this.

check_for_template_tags_with_the_same_name collects libraries from TEMPLATES OPTIONS['libraries'] and from get_template_tag_modules() into the same dict; the duplicate (same path twice) report arises because entries were stored without deduplication — using `libraries = defaultdict(set)` (with .add) dedupes identical paths so only truly different modules trigger the warning.

In DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env (postgresql/client.py), the extra parameters are added with args.extend(parameters) before the dbname is appended (args += [dbname]), so the database name comes last, after all options.

That template is never really used, because the form renders only hidden inputs. The fix is to set `template_name = "django/forms/div.html"` on `ManagementForm`, which avoids the warning.
